title: api: add request/response API-version negotiation and backcompat shim for openai-compat
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We are rolling out a v2 request/response shape for streaming envelopes and structured outputs (tool/function calling shape changes). To avoid breaking existing OpenAI-compatible clients we introduce a server-side API-version negotiation layer plus a backcompat shim that translates between v1 (current clients) and v2 (internal/new SDKs). This PR implements the negotiation middleware, transformation shims, docs, tests, and a controlled rollout plan.

What this PR does: Adds X-Redwood-Api-Version header support (clients may send e.g. 'v1', 'v2-beta'). If header absent we fall back to best-effort negotiation using Accept and OpenAI-Compat hinting. Introduces a compat shim that: 1) rewrites incoming v1-style function_call payloads into v2 structured-request internals; 2) converts internal v2 structured outputs back into v1 streaming envelopes for clients that requested v1; 3) preserves streaming chunk framing semantics for older clients while enabling chunk-level structured metadata for v2 clients.

Compatibility guarantees: The shim ensures no breaking changes for clients that do not opt into v2. For v2 clients (header or SDK opt-in) they will receive the new schema (structured output objects in the streaming event payload, explicit 'schema_version':'2' in response metadata). Deprecation policy: We will mark the implicit v1 wire format as deprecated in 6 months. Servers emit a deprecation warning header 'X-Redwood-Deprecation: wire-v1 (2026-08-15)'.

Implementation details (high-level): Middleware: server/api/version_middleware.go implements negotiation and attaches a request context flag. Shim: compat/openai/shim_v1_to_v2.go and shim_v2_to_v1.go perform deterministic translations; they are stateless and tested. Streaming: streaming/stream_adapter.go applies envelope conversion with backpressure awareness and keeps old frame types for v1 to avoid breaking clients that parse chunk separators. SDK changes: small helpers in sdk/python/openai_compat.py and sdk/typescript/openai-compat.ts expose an opt-in API to set the header. Docs: docs/migrations/api-versioning.md documents the header, examples, and migration checklist.

Rollout & safety: Feature-flagged behind 'api.version_negotiation' (FF toggled on for internal traffic). We will canary the header-less behavior to 5% of production traffic; when stable expand to 50% then full. Metrics added: redwood.api.version.negotiation.success, redwood.api.compat.translation.failures, redwood.streaming.frame_loss_rate. Alerts: translation failure rate >0.1% triggers P1.

Testing: Unit tests for both shim directions, integration tests against python/typescript compat SDKs, streaming e2e tests that assert old clients receive identical v1 chunks, and v2 clients receive structured JSON events. A flaky streaming test was stabilized by adding deterministic chunk timing. CI summary: all unit and integration checks passed on main; streaming-e2e required a retry but passed on rerun.

Migration notes for customers: If you want v2 early, set header 'X-Redwood-Api-Version: v2-beta' or upgrade to the new SDK helpers. If you rely on function_call semantics from OpenAI-compat, keep using v1 for now; the shim preserves behavior. We will publish a migration guide and sample code snippets in the docs PR.

Checklist: - [x] middleware + shim implementation - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs update - [x] metrics & alerts - [x] rollout plan

Risks and mitigations: translation mismatches are possible for user-defined tool schemas; we fail-open by returning a structured-degeneration placeholder and incrementing translation failure metric so we can triage and add targeted shims.

Related: ENG-1427 defines versioning scheme; ENG-1503 tracked streaming envelope changes.

Summary: This PR provides a pragmatic path to evolve our API surface without breaking existing OpenAI-compat clients by negotiating wire schema and applying a reversible translation layer. The shim is designed to be removed once clients have migrated and v1 is EOL.
commits: feat(api): add version negotiation middleware and header handling
feat(compat): implement v1->v2 and v2->v1 deterministic shims
test(streaming): add e2e streaming schema tests for both versions
chore(sdk): expose header helper in python and ts SDKs
review_comments: Arjun: Can the shim preserve 'finish_reason' semantics used by many downstream parsers? Please add unit tests for that case.
Author(Maya): Added tests for finish_reason and preserved behavior in shim_v2_to_v1; also added a regression e2e.
Sofia: We need an ops playbook entry for translation failures and how to roll back the FF.

release_notes: Add API version negotiation and backcompat shim: clients may opt into v2 via X-Redwood-Api-Version header. Default behavior preserved for v1 clients. See docs/migrations/api-versioning.md for migration steps.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: internal -> 5% canary -> 50% -> 100%. Header-driven opt-in available immediately. Monitor redwood.api.compat.translation.failures and redwood.streaming.frame_loss_rate.
tests_summary: Unit tests for shim logic, integration tests with Python/TS compat helpers, streaming e2e validating chunking/schema semantics. All tests passed in CI after one rerun for flaky streaming-e2e.
regression_risks: Translation edge-cases for complex user tool schemas; mitigated by non-breaking placeholder responses and metrics to quickly identify cases.
notes_for_ops: When enabling canary, ensure the feature flag 'api.version_negotiation' is scoped and SLOs for streaming latency are observed. If translation failures spike, rollback FF and open ENG-1503 follow-up.
